items.s: Look! The robot ___ across the playground.
items.h: Look! means it is happening now: the robot is rolling.

items.s: We ___ football when it started to rain.
items.h: Use were + -ing for something that was going on: we were playing.

items.s: I haven't ___ my cousins since last summer.
items.h: After have or haven't, use the past participle: I haven't seen.

items.s: Next week our class ___ plant trees in the park.
items.h: Next week is in the future, so use will: our class will plant.

items.s: Look at those dark clouds! It's going to ___.
items.h: After going to, use the plain verb: it's going to rain.

items.s: My brother ___ his bike to school every day.
items.h: Every day means a habit. With he, she or it, add s: he rides.

items.s: While I was reading, my cat ___ on my lap.
items.h: Both things were going on in the past: the cat was sleeping.

items.s: Have you ever ___ in a hot-air balloon?
items.h: After have, use the past participle: fly, flew, have flown.

items.s: We have ___ waiting here since nine o'clock.
items.h: Since tells us how long: we have been waiting.

items.s: I really enjoy ___ cakes with my grandad.
items.h: After enjoy, use the -ing form: I enjoy baking.

items.s: Zara promised ___ me with my project.
items.h: After promise, use to + verb: she promised to help.

items.s: When we got home, Dad had already ___ dinner.
items.h: After had, use the past participle: Dad had cooked.

items.s: Next summer we are going to ___ to Scotland.
items.h: After going to, use the plain verb: we are going to travel.

items.s: The Earth ___ round the Sun once a year.
items.h: Facts use the present. With it, go becomes goes: the Earth goes.

items.s: Water ___ at 100 degrees Celsius.
items.h: A fact about water uses the present with s: water boils.

items.s: Right now, Grandma ___ a cake in the kitchen.
items.h: Right now means it is happening: Grandma is baking.

items.s: When Grandad was young, he ___ to walk to school.
items.h: Used to tells us what often happened in the past.

items.s: If the sun ___ out, we will go to the beach.
items.h: If + present, then will: if the sun comes out, we will go.

items.s: I've ___ my homework, so now I can play outside.
items.h: I've means I have, so use the past participle: I've finished.

items.s: At this time yesterday, we ___ swimming in the sea.
items.h: Yesterday is past, and we goes with were: we were swimming.

items.s: Mum asked me ___ the table for dinner.
items.h: After asked me, use to + verb: she asked me to set the table.

items.s: We are looking forward to ___ the zoo.
items.h: Looking forward to is followed by -ing: looking forward to visiting.

items.s: My sister ___ the piano for three years now.
items.h: For three years up to now, use has + past participle: has played.

items.s: Hurry up! The train ___ in five minutes.
items.h: Timetables use the present: the train leaves at ten.

items.s: This castle was ___ nine hundred years ago.
items.h: Was + past participle says what was done: it was built.

items.s: Our teacher made us ___ the poem twice.
items.h: After made us, use the plain verb with no to: made us read.

items.s: Yesterday Dad ___ me how to fly a kite.
items.h: Teach is irregular: today I teach, yesterday I taught.

items.s: Sam ___ the bus just before the doors closed.
items.h: Catch is irregular: catch, caught, have caught.

items.s: The pond ___ over during the frosty night.
items.h: Freeze is irregular: the pond froze. Frozen needs was or had.

items.s: Last week our class ___ poems about the sea.
items.h: Write is irregular: write, wrote, have written.

items.s: At the party, Dad ___ a silly pirate costume.
items.h: Wear is irregular: wear, wore, have worn.

items.s: The tiny seed ___ into a tall sunflower.
items.h: Grow is irregular: grow, grew, has grown.

items.s: The baby ___ up when the doorbell rang.
items.h: Wake is irregular: wake, woke, has woken.

items.s: Last summer we ___ in the sea every day.
items.h: Swim is irregular: swim, swam, have swum.

items.s: The bell ___ and everyone ran out to play.
items.h: Ring is irregular: the bell rang. Rung needs has or had.

items.s: Last week Mum ___ me a new reading book.
items.h: Buy is irregular: buy, bought, have bought.

items.s: A rabbit ___ a burrow under the hedge yesterday.
items.h: Dig is irregular: dig, dug, has dug.

items.s: I ___ my water bottle at home this morning.
items.h: Leave is irregular: this morning I left it at home.

items.s: Whoosh! Noah ___ out all ten birthday candles!
items.h: Blow is irregular: blow, blew, has blown.

items.s: Yesterday the robot ___ a picture of a horse.
items.h: Draw is irregular: draw, drew, has drawn.

items.s: Last night I ___ for ten whole hours!
items.h: Sleep is irregular: last night I slept.

items.s: I ___ the test would be hard, but it was easy.
items.h: Think is irregular: think, thought, have thought.

items.s: Yesterday our class ___ a song in assembly.
items.h: Sing is irregular: sing, sang, have sung.

items.s: He ___ the ball so far it went over the wall!
items.h: Throw is irregular: throw, threw, has thrown.

items.s: Last night our dog ___ my homework!
items.h: Eat is irregular: eat, ate, has eaten.

items.s: Our class ___ the quiz at the summer fair!
items.h: Win is irregular: win, won, have won.

items.s: Everyone in my family ___ curly hair.
items.h: Everyone means each person, so it takes has: everyone has.

items.s: One of my friends ___ from Wales.
items.h: The subject is one (not friends), so use is: one of them is.

items.s: My friends and I ___ going to the cinema.
items.h: My friends and I means we, so use are: we are going.

items.s: There ___ five ducks swimming on the pond.
items.h: Five ducks is plural, so use there are.

items.s: Each of the players ___ a number on their shirt.
items.h: Each means every single one, so use has: each player has.

items.s: The box of crayons ___ on the top shelf.
items.h: The subject is the box (one), not the crayons: the box is.

items.s: Maths ___ always been my favourite subject.
items.h: Maths is one subject even though it ends in s: maths has.

items.s: ___ your brother play the violin?
items.h: With he, she or it, ask with does: does your brother play?

items.s: ___ the twins enjoy swimming?
items.h: The twins is plural, so ask with do: do the twins enjoy it?

items.s: My grandparents ___ been to Australia twice.
items.h: Grandparents is plural, so use have: they have been.

items.s: The news ___ exciting: we're going to the zoo!
items.h: News is one thing, even with an s: the news is good.

items.s: Yesterday the roads ___ covered in snow.
items.h: Yesterday is past, and roads is plural: the roads were.

items.s: A lot of people ___ watching the parade yesterday.
items.h: People is plural and yesterday is past: people were.

items.s: My scissors ___ in the top drawer.
items.h: Scissors is always plural, like trousers: the scissors are.

items.s: Every dog in the park ___ wagging its tail.
items.h: Every dog means each one, so use was: every dog was.

items.s: In autumn, the ___ on the trees turn red and gold.
items.h: Leaf changes f to v and adds es: one leaf, two leaves.

items.s: Please put the forks and ___ in the drawer.
items.h: Knife changes f to v: one knife, two knives.

items.s: The firefighters were real ___ that day.
items.h: Hero adds es: one hero, two heroes.

items.s: We need six ___ to make the soup.
items.h: Potato adds es: one potato, two potatoes.

items.s: We shouted and heard our ___ in the cave.
items.h: Echo adds es, like hero and potato: echoes.

items.s: Two ___ make a whole.
items.h: Half changes f to v: one half, two halves.

items.s: The baker made ten ___ of bread.
items.h: Loaf changes f to v: one loaf, two loaves.

items.s: Two fluffy ___ were munching grass on the hill.
items.h: Sheep stays the same: one sheep, two sheep.

items.s: Two ___ waddled across the farmyard.
items.h: Goose changes its vowels: one goose, two geese.

items.s: Our puppy has lost two of its baby ___.
items.h: Tooth changes its vowels: one tooth, many teeth.

items.s: My little sisters both love fairy ___.
items.h: After a consonant, y changes to ies: story, stories.

items.s: The farmer's two ___ pulled the heavy cart.
items.h: Ox has an old plural with en: one ox, two oxen.

items.s: Our school has two pet ___ called Bubble and Squeak.
items.h: Mouse changes its middle: one mouse, two mice.

items.s: Three ___ won medals in the race.
items.h: One woman, two women. Never add s to women.

items.s: People say that cats have nine ___.
items.h: Life changes f to v: one life, nine lives.

items.s: The two ___ cooked a feast in the kitchen.
items.h: Chef just adds s. Not every f word changes to ves!

items.s: The ___ swung from tree to tree.
items.h: After a vowel, keep the y and add s: monkey, monkeys.

items.s: We visited three ___ on our holiday.
items.h: After a consonant, y changes to ies: country, countries.

items.s: We waited for ___ hour at the bus stop.
items.h: In hour the h is silent, so it starts with a vowel sound: an.

items.s: My cousin studies at ___ university in Wales.
items.h: University starts with a 'you' sound, so use a: a university.

items.s: Have you got ___ crayons I could borrow?
items.h: Use any in questions about plurals: have you got any crayons?

items.s: Who was ___ first person to walk on the Moon?
items.h: Use the with first, last and best: the first person.

items.s: I'd like ___ grapes in my lunchbox, please.
items.h: Use some with plurals when you ask for things: some grapes.

items.s: ___ elephant never forgets, people say.
items.h: Elephant starts with a vowel sound, so use an: an elephant.

items.s: She is ___ honest girl who never tells fibs.
items.h: In honest the h is silent, so it starts with a vowel sound: an.

items.s: There isn't ___ water in the paddling pool.
items.h: Use any after not with words like water: there isn't any.

items.s: Dad and ___ made pancakes for breakfast.
items.h: Take away 'Dad and': I made pancakes, not me made pancakes.

items.s: Our teacher gave a sticker to Ben and ___.
items.h: Take away 'Ben and': she gave a sticker to me, not to I.

items.s: That's the girl ___ kite got stuck in the tree.
items.h: Whose shows that something belongs to someone: whose kite.

items.s: This is the machine ___ makes ice cream.
items.h: Use which (or that) for things and who for people.

items.s: Mrs Patel is the teacher ___ runs chess club.
items.h: Use who for people: the teacher who runs chess club.

items.s: I taught ___ to juggle with three oranges.
items.h: When you do something to you, use myself: I taught myself.

items.s: The robot can charge ___ when its battery is low.
items.h: The robot does it to itself. Itself has just one s.

items.s: The blue bike is ___ and the red one is yours.
items.h: Yours, mine, hers and ours stand alone: it is mine.

items.s: That jacket isn't mine. It must be ___.
items.h: Hers never has an apostrophe: the jacket is hers.

items.s: The twins said the drawing was ___.
items.h: Theirs means it belongs to them. It has no apostrophe.

items.s: Let's tidy the room ___ instead of asking for help.
items.h: We do it with no help, so use ourselves: one self, two selves.

items.s: Between you and ___, I think the cake is too salty.
items.h: After between, use me, not I: between you and me.

items.s: ___ is your favourite planet, Mars or Jupiter?
items.h: Use which when you choose between things: which planet?

items.s: ___ muddy footprints are these on the floor?
items.h: Whose asks who something belongs to: whose footprints?

items.s: Ravi and Ella love art. ___ painted a huge mural.
items.h: They does the action: they painted it. Them comes after a verb.

items.s: Did you make that model all by ___?
items.h: All by yourself means with no help from anyone else.

items.s: Lucy lent me ___ ruler because I'd lost mine.
items.h: Use her before a noun: her ruler. Hers stands alone.

items.s: At the party, the girls helped ___ to more cake.
items.h: They did it for them, so use themselves (never theirselves).

items.s: Grandma read ___ a story before bed.
items.h: After a verb like read, use us, not we: she read us a story.

items.s: My little brother is afraid ___ spiders.
items.h: We say afraid of: afraid of spiders, afraid of the dark.

items.s: Priya is brilliant ___ maths and chess.
items.h: We are good at or brilliant at something.

items.s: Ali is really interested ___ dinosaurs.
items.h: We say interested in: interested in dinosaurs.

items.s: Mum was so proud ___ my science project.
items.h: We say proud of: proud of you, proud of my work.

items.s: Our school trip is ___ the twelfth of May.
items.h: Use on with dates and days: on the twelfth of May.

items.s: Owls are awake ___ night and sleep by day.
items.h: We say at night, but in the morning and in the evening.

items.s: Hurry up, or we'll be late ___ school!
items.h: We say late for: late for school, late for dinner.

items.s: This sandwich is full ___ crunchy salad.
items.h: We say full of: a box full of toys.

items.s: We travelled to Paris ___ train.
items.h: Use by for how you travel: by train, by bus, by car.

items.s: Please look ___ my hamster while I'm away.
items.h: Look after means take care of: look after my hamster.

items.s: I'm really excited ___ the school trip!
items.h: We say excited about: excited about the trip.

items.s: This song reminds me ___ our summer holiday.
items.h: Something reminds you of something else.

items.s: Who does this muddy football belong ___?
items.h: Things belong to people: it belongs to me.

items.s: My cousin is very keen ___ rock climbing.
items.h: Keen on means really liking something: keen on climbing.

items.s: The castle is famous ___ its tall towers.
items.h: We say famous for: famous for its towers.

items.s: We sat and listened ___ the birds singing.
items.h: We always listen to something: listen to the birds.

items.s: Our new classroom is similar ___ the old one.
items.h: We say similar to: similar to the old one.

items.s: I broke the vase by accident, not ___ purpose.
items.h: On purpose means you meant to do it. By accident means you didn't.

items.s: The teacher divided the class ___ four teams.
items.h: We divide or split things into groups.

items.s: Omar apologised ___ spilling the paint.
items.h: We apologise for something: sorry for the mess.

items.s: We arrived ___ the airport just in time.
items.h: Arrive at a place like a station or airport, never arrive to.

items.s: I prefer swimming ___ running.
items.h: After prefer, use to: I prefer apples to pears.

items.s: Plants depend ___ sunlight and water.
items.h: We say depend on: plants depend on sunlight.

items.s: The players lifted ___ trophy high in the air.
items.h: Their means belonging to them: their trophy.

items.s: ___ going to the museum after lunch.
items.h: They're is short for they are: they are going.

items.s: Put the box over ___, next to the door.
items.h: There is a place, like here: over there.

items.s: The robot lifted ___ arm and waved.
items.h: Its (no apostrophe) means belonging to it: its arm.

items.s: ___ time for lunch! Wash your hands, please.
items.h: It's is short for it is: it is time for lunch.

items.s: Don't forget ___ coat; it's cold outside!
items.h: Your means belonging to you: your coat.

items.s: I think ___ going to love this book!
items.h: You're is short for you are: you are going to love it.

items.s: ___ turn is it to feed the fish?
items.h: Whose asks who something belongs to: whose turn?

items.s: ___ coming to the party on Saturday?
items.h: Who's is short for who is: who is coming?

items.s: ___ did you put my football boots?
items.h: Where asks about a place: where are my boots?

items.s: I'm going to ___ my new jumper today.
items.h: Wear is what you do with clothes: wear a jumper.

items.s: We ___ all very tired after the long walk.
items.h: Were is the past of are: we were tired.

items.s: The classroom was so ___ you could hear a pin drop.
items.h: Quiet (ends -et) means not noisy. Quite means fairly.

items.s: The film was ___ long, but I enjoyed it.
items.h: Quite (ends -te) means fairly: quite long. Quiet means not noisy.

items.s: Everyone went swimming ___ Zoe, who was away.
items.h: Except means apart from: everyone except Zoe.

items.s: Please ___ this small gift as a thank-you.
items.h: Accept means take something that is offered to you.

items.s: The top shelf is ___ high for me to reach.
items.h: Too (two o's) means more than you want: too high.

items.s: The rain didn't ___ our plans for the picnic.
items.h: Affect is a verb: to change something. Effect is a noun.

items.s: On the way home, we walked ___ the old church.
items.h: Past tells you where: we walked past it. Passed is a verb.

items.s: We are not ___ to run in the corridor.
items.h: Allowed means let: we are not allowed. Aloud means out loud.

items.s: Please read the poem ___ to the class.
items.h: Aloud means so that others can hear: read aloud.

items.s: What will the ___ be like tomorrow?
items.h: Weather is sun, rain and wind. Whether means if.

items.s: I don't know ___ to wear my coat or not.
items.h: Whether means if: whether or not.

items.s: Squeeze the ___ to stop your bike.
items.h: A brake stops a bike or car. A break is a rest.

items.s: Can you ___ a thank-you letter to Grandma?
items.h: Write is what you do with a pen: write a letter.

items.s: The ball flew ___ the open window.
items.h: Through means in one side and out the other.

items.s: Can I give you some ___ about your project?
items.h: Advice (with c) is the noun. Advise (with s) is the verb.

items.s: I need to ___ my spellings every night.
items.h: In British English the verb is practise (s). The noun is practice.

items.s: For ___, we had apple crumble and custard.
items.h: Dessert is a pudding. Remember: two s for 'sweet stuff'.

items.s: My dog is much bigger ___ my cat.
items.h: Use than to compare things: bigger than. Then means next.

items.s: Don't ___ your gloves on the school trip!
items.h: Lose (one o) means not have it any more. Loose means not tight.

items.s: For breakfast, I like a bowl of ___.
items.h: Cereal is breakfast food. A serial is a story told in parts.

items.s: Pizza is my ___ food in the whole world.
items.h: Favourite has 'our' like colour: fav-our-ite.

items.s: Do you ___ in aliens?
items.h: Never believe a lie: there is a lie hiding in believe.

items.s: Twins can look alike but have ___ hobbies.
items.h: Different has double f and ends -ent: dif-fer-ent.

items.s: Please keep the red and blue pens ___.
items.h: There is a rat in separate: sep-a-rat-e.

items.s: Valentine's Day is on the 14th of ___.
items.h: February has a hidden r after Feb: Feb-ru-ary.

items.s: Our school ___ has a cosy reading corner.
items.h: Library has two r's: lib-rar-y.

items.s: Shh! The party is a ___ for Grandma.
items.h: Surprise starts with sur, like surf: sur-prise.

items.s: The sunset over the sea was ___.
items.h: Beautiful starts b-e-a-u and ends with just one l.

items.s: Water is ___ for all living things.
items.h: Necessary has one collar and two sleeves: one c, two s.

items.s: The nurse took my ___ with a thermometer.
items.h: Say every part: tem-per-a-ture.

items.s: Carrots are a crunchy, healthy ___.
items.h: Say every part: veg-e-ta-ble.

items.s: We went to a ___ for Grandma's birthday lunch.
items.h: Restaurant is rest + au + rant: rest-au-rant.

items.s: Clap along to the ___ of the drum.
items.h: Rhythm Helps Your Two Hips Move: r-h-y-t-h-m.

items.s: We waited in a long ___ for the roller coaster.
items.h: Queue is q followed by u-e-u-e: q-u-e-u-e.

items.s: Our ___ next door has a lovely garden.
items.h: Neighbour is neigh (like a horse) + bour.

items.s: I love all animals, ___ penguins.
items.h: Especially is es (not ex) + special + ly.

items.s: I felt ___ when I forgot my lines in the play.
items.h: Embarrassed has double r and double s: em-bar-rassed.

items.s: The ___ kitten unrolled all the wool.
items.h: Mischievous has no i before the ous: mis-chie-vous.

items.s: December is the ___ month of the year.
items.h: Twelfth keeps the f sound from twelve: twelf + th.

items.s: We must protect our ___ and stop litter.
items.h: Environment has iron in the middle: env-iron-ment.

items.s: You need a passport to visit a ___ country.
items.h: Foreign breaks the i before e rule: for-eign.

items.s: Ten times four is ___.
items.h: Four has a u, but forty does not: f-o-r-t-y.

items.s: The ___ of a giraffe can be over five metres.
items.h: Height is h + eight: h-eight.

items.s: We sailed around the bay on a ___.
items.h: Yacht is a strange one: y-a-c-h-t, with a silent ch.

items.s: We camped on a small ___ in the middle of the lake.
items.h: Island has a silent s: is-land.

items.s: The first puzzle was easy, but the second was ___.
items.h: But shows a change: the opposite of easy is difficult.

items.s: I'm the oldest child; my baby sister is the ___.
items.h: The opposite of oldest is youngest.

items.s: My bag was heavy, but Ava's was as ___ as a feather.
items.h: The opposite of heavy is light: as light as a feather.

items.s: The shop opens at nine and ___ at five.
items.h: The opposite of opens is closes.

items.s: Don't forget your PE kit; try to ___ it!
items.h: The opposite of forget is remember.

items.s: Our old house was tiny, but our new one is ___.
items.h: Enormous means very big, the opposite of tiny.

items.s: Lions are wild, but our pet cat is ___.
items.h: Tame animals are used to people: the opposite of wild.

items.s: The river was deep in the middle but ___ near the edge.
items.h: Shallow water is not deep: the opposite of deep.

items.s: I like to arrive early, but my brother is always ___.
items.h: The opposite of early is late.

items.s: The start of the film was dull, but the ___ was exciting.
items.h: The opposite of the start or beginning is the ending.

items.s: We didn't lose the match. We ___!
items.h: The opposite of lose is win, and the past of win is won.

items.s: The puppy was asleep, but now it's wide ___.
items.h: The opposite of asleep is awake: wide awake!

items.s: Mum's kitchen is tidy, but my bedroom is ___.
items.h: The opposite of tidy is messy (or untidy).

items.s: A person who writes books is called an ___.
items.h: An author writes books. An illustrator draws the pictures.

items.s: A scientist who studies the stars is an ___.
items.h: An astronomer studies stars. An astronaut travels into space.

items.s: Bees collect ___ from flowers to make honey.
items.h: Nectar is the sweet juice in flowers that bees turn into honey.

items.s: An animal that eats only plants is a ___.
items.h: Herbivores eat plants. Carnivores eat meat. Omnivores eat both.

items.s: When water boils, it turns into ___.
items.h: Boiling turns water into steam. Freezing turns it into ice.

items.s: We use a ___ to look at tiny things like cells.
items.h: A microscope makes tiny things look big. Micro means small.

items.s: A ___ shows old and precious things from history.
items.h: A museum keeps and shows interesting things from the past.

items.s: A ___ tells you how to make a cake.
items.h: A recipe gives the ingredients and the steps for cooking.

items.s: Something that is ___ cannot be seen.
items.h: In- means not, so invisible means not able to be seen.

items.s: A shape with eight sides is an ___.
items.h: Octo means eight: an octopus has eight arms!

items.s: Lena loves exploring new places; she's so ___.
items.h: Adventurous people love trying new and exciting things.

items.s: Tom always shares his sweets. He's very ___.
items.h: Generous people like giving and sharing.

items.s: A ___ is a big group of bees flying together.
items.h: Bees fly in a swarm. Sheep are in a flock and cows in a herd.

items.s: The ___ of a river is where it begins.
items.h: A river starts at its source and ends at its mouth.

items.s: A ___ is a mountain that can erupt with lava.
items.h: A volcano can erupt: hot melted rock called lava comes out.

items.s: I was ___ to see my cousin; I gave her a big hug!
items.h: Delighted means very happy.

items.s: An ___ is a book full of maps.
items.h: An atlas is a book of maps of the world.

items.s: Swallows ___ to Africa every autumn.
items.h: To migrate is to travel far away for the season.

items.s: Hedgehogs ___ through the cold winter months.
items.h: Animals that hibernate sleep through the winter.

items.s: A ___ is a word that means the same as another.
items.h: Synonyms mean the same (big, large). Antonyms are opposites.

items.s: Jupiter is the ___ planet in our Solar System.
items.h: Short word, short vowel: double the g and add -est: biggest.

items.s: Today is ___ than yesterday, so wear shorts.
items.h: Comparing two days? Use -er with than: hot, hotter.

items.s: My new bike is much ___ than my old one.
items.h: Good is irregular: good, better, best.

items.s: That was the ___ joke I've ever heard!
items.h: Change y to i and add -est: funny, funnier, funniest.

items.s: Of all the runners, Mia is the ___.
items.h: Comparing more than two? Use the + -est: the fastest.

items.s: The weather today is even ___ than yesterday.
items.h: Bad is irregular: bad, worse, worst.

items.s: Kai lives ___ from school than I do.
items.h: Far is irregular: far, further, furthest.

items.s: Running is ___ tiring than walking.
items.h: Long words use more with than: more tiring than.

items.s: Science is the ___ interesting subject of all!
items.h: Long words use the most for the top one: the most interesting.

items.s: My school bag is ___ than my lunchbox.
items.h: Change y to i and add -er: heavy, heavier.

items.s: My brother is three years ___ than me.
items.h: Use older with than. Elder only goes before a noun: my elder sister.

items.s: Your sandcastle is as tall ___ mine!
items.h: To say two things are equal, use as ... as: as tall as.

items.s: I have ___ homework than my sister.
items.h: Use less for things you can't count, like homework or water.

items.s: A giraffe's neck is ___ than a horse's.
items.h: Comparing two things? Use -er and than: longer than.

items.s: The giant redwood is the ___ tree on Earth.
items.h: For the top one of a whole group, use the + -est: the tallest.

items.s: Leo wore his wellies ___ the field was muddy.
items.h: Because gives the reason: the mud is why he wore wellies.

items.s: ___ the water was cold, we still went swimming.
items.h: Although shows a surprise: it was cold, but we still swam.

items.s: You can't go out to play ___ you tidy your room.
items.h: Unless means if not: no playing if you don't tidy up.

items.s: The puppy looked hungry, ___ we filled its bowl.
items.h: So tells you what happened as a result.

items.s: ___ I was walking to school, I saw a rainbow.
items.h: While means during the time that something happens.

items.s: Wait here ___ the bell rings.
items.h: Until means up to the time when: wait until the bell rings.

items.s: Always wash your hands ___ you eat your lunch.
items.h: Before means earlier than: wash your hands first.

items.s: I'll lend you my bike ___ you promise to be careful.
items.h: If sets a condition: you can have it only if you promise.

items.s: Shall we play football ___ go for a bike ride?
items.h: Use or when there is a choice: this or that?

items.s: We've lived in this house ___ I was a baby.
items.h: Since tells you when something started: since I was a baby.

items.s: I'll call you as ___ as I get home.
items.h: As soon as means straight after: as soon as I get home.

items.s: Cats love to nap, ___ puppies love to play.
items.h: Whereas shows how two things are different, like but.

items.s: She won the race ___ she had a sore foot.
items.h: Even though shows a surprise: she won with a sore foot!

items.s: Take an umbrella ___ it rains later.
items.h: In case means so you are ready if it happens.

items.s: Tidy up now, ___ you won't have time to play.
items.h: Or can mean if not: tidy up now, or there's no time to play.

items.s: Speak quietly ___ you don't wake the baby.
items.h: So that gives the purpose: so the baby keeps sleeping.

items.s: You can have ___ the cake or the ice cream.
items.h: Either goes with or: either this or that.

items.s: It was ___ cold that the lake froze.
items.h: So + describing word + that: so cold that it froze.

items.s: You ___ run near the pool; it's slippery.
items.h: Mustn't means it is not allowed: you mustn't run.

items.s: I ___ find my shoes, so I was late.
items.h: Couldn't is the past of can't: I couldn't find them.

items.s: Take a coat. It ___ rain later.
items.h: May shows something is possible: it may rain.

items.s: You ___ eat lots of vegetables to stay healthy.
items.h: Should gives good advice: you should eat vegetables.

items.s: ___ I have another biscuit, please?
items.h: Ask politely with may, can or could: may I have one?

items.s: We ___ hurry, or we'll miss the train!
items.h: Must means it is really necessary: we must hurry.

items.s: You ___ bring a packed lunch; lunch is provided.
items.h: Needn't means it isn't necessary: you needn't bring one.

items.s: If I had wings, I ___ fly to school.
items.h: For imaginary things, use if + past, then would.

items.s: It's Saturday, so I don't ___ get up early.
items.h: Don't have to means it isn't needed: I don't have to get up.

items.s: You ___ to say thank you for a present.
items.h: Only ought is followed by to: you ought to say thank you.

items.s: My dad ___ play the guitar really well.
items.h: Can never takes s or to: he can play.

items.s: I'm not sure, but I ___ go to the party.
items.h: Might shows you are not sure: I might go.

items.s: ___ you help me carry these books, please?
items.h: Could you...? is a polite way to ask for help.

items.s: Carry the eggs ___ so they don't break.
items.h: To say how you do something, add -ly: careful, carefully.

items.s: We were filled with ___ when we won the cup.
items.h: After filled with, we need a noun: happy becomes happiness.

items.s: The ___ of the light bulb changed the world.
items.h: After the, we need a noun: invent becomes invention.

items.s: Her ___ to animals makes her a great vet.
items.h: After her, we need a noun: kind becomes kindness.

items.s: The firefighter won a medal for her ___.
items.h: After her, we need a noun: brave becomes bravery.

items.s: We jumped up and down with ___!
items.h: After with, we need a noun: excite becomes excitement.

items.s: Use your ___ to write a story about dragons.
items.h: After your, we need a noun: imagine becomes imagination.

items.s: This sofa is very ___ to sit on.
items.h: Add -able to make a describing word: comfort, comfortable.

items.s: A fish can't climb a tree; it's ___!
items.h: Im- means not: impossible means not possible.

items.s: Poof! The rabbit ___ into thin air.
items.h: Dis- makes the opposite: appear, disappear.

items.s: Our school play was a huge ___.
items.h: After a huge, we need a noun: success.

items.s: Mia made a quick ___ and chose the red one.
items.h: After a quick, we need a noun: decide becomes decision.

items.s: The brave ___ sailed off to find a new land.
items.h: Add -er for the person who does it: explore, explorer.

items.s: Grandad spoke ___ to the nervous pony.
items.h: To say how he spoke, use -ly: gentle becomes gently.

items.s: We were amazed by the ___ of the waterfall.
items.h: After the, we need a noun: beautiful becomes beauty.

items.s: Please don't ___ a noise while Grandma naps.
items.h: We make a noise, make a mess and make a cake.

items.s: I always ___ my best in tests.
items.h: We do our best, do homework and do the washing-up.

items.s: Let's ___ a photo of the sunset.
items.h: We take a photo, take a turn and take a break.

items.s: We ___ a great time at the party.
items.h: We have fun and have a great time.

items.s: It's hard to ___ a choice between two puppies!
items.h: We make a choice, make a decision and make a plan.

items.s: Don't forget to ___ attention in class.
items.h: We pay attention: we listen and watch carefully.

items.s: I ___ a mistake in my spelling test.
items.h: We make mistakes, not do them: I made a mistake.

items.s: Can you ___ a secret?
items.h: We keep a secret, keep a promise and keep calm.

items.s: Please ___ the truth about the broken vase.
items.h: We tell the truth, tell a story and tell a joke.

items.s: Can you ___ me a hand with these boxes?
items.h: Give me a hand means help me.

items.s: Did you ___ a cold from your brother?
items.h: We catch a cold, just like we catch a ball.

items.s: If we don't leave now, we'll ___ the bus!
items.h: We miss a bus or train when we're too late to get on.

items.s: Learning to swim was a piece of ___!
items.h: A piece of cake means something is very easy.

items.s: I'm feeling a bit under the ___ today.
items.h: Under the weather means feeling a little unwell.

items.s: Grandad has a ___ tooth; he loves cake.
items.h: Having a sweet tooth means you love sweet food.

items.s: We're all in the same ___, so let's help each other.
items.h: In the same boat means in the same situation.

items.s: We only go to the cinema once in a blue ___.
items.h: Once in a blue moon means very rarely.

items.s: Keep your ___ up — you'll do better next time!
items.h: Keep your chin up means stay cheerful.

items.s: Don't worry, it's not rocket ___; it's easy!
items.h: It's not rocket science means it's not hard to do.

items.s: The new pupil stayed as cool as a ___.
items.h: As cool as a cucumber means calm and relaxed.
